criterion: The response names estimate_gas_to_fulfill in crates/boundless-market/src/prover_utils/mod.rs as the pricing-time routine that produces the inflated fulfillment gas figure the refusal turns on.

The response names price_order in crates/boundless-market/src/prover_utils/mod.rs as the routine that turns that estimate into the order's gas cost by multiplying it by the current gas price and stores it on the order.

The response traces the decline of a funded order to the gas cost being compared against the request's own offer maxPrice, naming either check_available_balances in crates/broker/src/order_pricer/helpers.rs or the post-preflight re-check inside price_order in crates/boundless-market/src/prover_utils/mod.rs as the branch that skips it.

The response names calculate_exec_limits in crates/boundless-market/src/prover_utils/mod.rs as subtracting the same gas cost from the offer max price before deriving the cycle budget, which is why accepted orders get a smaller preflight allowance.
The response names submission_path_for_risc0_selector in crates/risc0-backend/src/lib.rs as the backend routine that routes the affected groth16-class selectors to SubmissionPath::Direct.

The response states that an order on the Direct submission path is set to ReadyForSubmission in crates/broker/src/order_processor/service.rs and so never enters the batcher, incurring no set-builder aggregation and no root submission.

The response names the near-identical estimate_gas_to_fulfill in crates/broker/src/utils/helpers.rs as a second copy of the same additive formula, separate from the pricing-time copy and differing by a journal-calldata term.

The response states that the pricing-time estimate classifies a request only by the proof type looked up in the supported-selector map and never consults the submission path or the router policy, so the classification that decides how an order settles and the one that decides what it is charged disagree.
The response states that adding groth16_verify_gas_estimate on top of fulfill_gas_estimate charges a second on-chain groth16 verification that an order settling on the direct path does not incur.
The response reports the estimate charged to an affected groth16-selector order as roughly 670,000 gas, the sum of the 420,000 base and the 250,000 groth16 term.

The response explains what separates the two groups of requests: a selector classified Inclusion or Any adds nothing beyond the base, and every selector that settles through the batcher falls in that group, so only the groth16-class selectors are overcharged.

The response names estimate_gas_usage_upper_bound in crates/boundless-market/src/request_builder/offer_layer.rs as innocent, because it runs while a requestor builds an offer and the broker crate never reaches the request_builder module.
The response names estimate_gas_to_lock in crates/broker/src/utils/helpers.rs as correct, since lock gas does not depend on how the order later settles.
The response clears both indexer uses of the same two gas constants, in crates/indexer/src/efficiency/service.rs and crates/indexer/src/market/service/status.rs, as reporting that decides nothing.

The response names apply_gas_limits in crates/broker/src/order_locker/service.rs as a consumer of the broker's lock-time copy that reserves the summed estimate against the signer's balance rather than against the request's max price.
The response lists file paths and routine names without explaining how they produce the reported refusal and the shrunken preflight allowance.
The response blames estimate_gas_usage_upper_bound in crates/boundless-market/src/request_builder/offer_layer.rs for the declined orders.
The response attributes the declined orders to the prover's gas-token balance being too low to cover the job.
The response identifies the batcher or the set-builder aggregation as the origin of the declined orders.
